text:
Sam (Finance): Quick question from a customer: they're asking how we bill for Private/VPC deployments where the compute lives in their cloud account but we manage the nodes. Specifically: network egress (NAT/EIP), GPU vendor licenses, and whether reserved/committed pricing can be applied. Any rules of thumb?

Renee (CloudOps): TL;DR: split by who owns the resource. If customer manages the VPC and resources, they get billed by their cloud account. If we create/own the infra, we treat cloud line items as pass-through or amortized reservation we control. Usually: EIP/NAT = pass-through at cost (no markup) if customer owns. If we own, cost+admin (5-10%).

Diego (SRE): GPU license nuance: many vendors invoice per node/socket to the payer on record. If license is required only for that dedicated customer and we bear the vendor invoice, we pass it through to them (we've shown it as a separate line item historically). If customer BYOL (they already have OEM licenses) we don't charge that fee.

Sam (Finance): Okay. What about reserved/commit discounts? Can customers in their VPC get our reserved pricing?

Priya (Acct Mgmt): Two options we present to customers: 1) Customer buys reservations in their account (they get cloud's committed rates directly) 2) Redwood-managed reservations: we reserve capacity in our account and expose instances to customer via peering or hosted network paths; we then amortize reservation cost monthly and invoice them. We require a minimum term (6/12 mo) and an explicit repayment clause.

Diego (SRE): Practically, if we reserve for them we must control tagging, monitoring, and have SLA clauses for capacity. Also need clear accounting so we don't double-bill committed discounts in our internal reporting.

Sam (Finance): Legal asked if we can add margin on vendor license fees. Any vendor restrictions?

LegalBot (automated): Note: Some OEM contracts disallow reselling licenses or require special reseller agreements. Check vendor TOS and reseller agreements. If restricted, pass through at cost and provide vendor invoice on request.

Renee (CloudOps): Region differences: egress/EIP/NAT cost varies a lot (e.g., eu-west vs us-east). Our invoice language should say "actual network egress and NAT charges billed at cost by region". For cross-region egress, add a callout — customer pays actuals.

CostBot (automated): SAMPLE BREAKDOWN (illustrative):
- Network (NAT/EIP/egress, eu-west-1) = $240/mo (tagged)
- Redwood-managed reservation amortized (4 p4 nodes) = $5,600/mo
- GPU vendor license = $400/mo (4 nodes @ $100/node)
- Operational fee = $624/mo (9% support and ops)
- TOTAL = $6,864/mo (rounded)

Sam (Finance): That format is helpful. We should present invoice lines as: Network (cloud line items), Compute reservation amortization (units + rate), GPU license fee (per-node), Service/ops fee. Keep itemization for audits.

Priya (Acct Mgmt): Sales playbook note: offer both BYO-reservation and Redwood-managed reservation. For Redwood-managed, require minimum commit, prepay option or monthly amortization, and a termination penalty if underused.

Diego (SRE): Operational note: for private VPCs where we manage nodes, ensure we can tag instances and export billing tags. If we can't, we need a mapping table and export of raw cloud invoices to reconcile.

Sam (Finance): Action items: 1) I'll draft sample invoice CSV and contract appendix text for pass-through vs managed reservations. 2) Legal to verify reseller permissions for NVIDIA/other GPU vendors. 3) CloudOps to create tagging and export checklist for customer-managed vs Redwood-managed infra. 4) Acct Mgmt to update the sales playbook with min commit and repayment terms.

Renee (CloudOps): One more: recommend a short FAQ entry in pricing page: "If Redwood manages resources in your VPC we may reserve capacity on your behalf and bill the amortized reservation cost; networking egress billed at cost by region; OEM licenses billed only if Redwood purchases them."

Sam (Finance): For on-prem/offline installs: If customer supplies OEM licenses and ownership is transferred or attested, we won't bill GPU license fees. Require written attestation or vendor transfer docs.

Diego (SRE): I'll upload the billing-tagger script and a sample reconciliation spreadsheet to the billing repo once legal confirms any vendor redactions.

Priya (Acct Mgmt): I'll prep two example contract snippets: (A) Pass-through: "Customer pays cloud network charges and OEM licenses directly unless Redwood purchases them on Customer's behalf" (B) Managed-reservation: "Redwood reserves capacity and invoices customer monthly for amortized reservation cost + ops fee; customer may prepay or commit for X months."

Sam (Finance): Great. I'll circulate drafts by EOD and open the legal ticket. Ping me for numbers to plug into the template.

Renee (CloudOps): +1 on the tagging guide — it'll speed reconciliations.

Diego (SRE): FYI, some vendors want to see customer usage to enable volume discounts. That may change whether we pass-through or include license in our product price. Keep Sales looped.

Sam (Finance): Thanks everyone. If no objections I'll mark this thread resolved after legal confirms reseller status. :white_check_mark:
